questions.question_english:
Examine the following statements about the Seventh Schedule and Educational Administration:
I. Before 1976, the Central Government had very limited legislative authority over school education.
II. The transfer of education to the Concurrent List enabled the creation of overarching national frameworks like the RTE Act.
III. The State Governments have lost all legislative powers over education after the 42nd Amendment. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
I and III
II and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Before 1976, school education was in the State List, restricting Central legislation. Shifting education to the Concurrent List enabled central laws like the RTE Act. Statement III is incorrect because State Governments retain broad legislative and administrative powers over education concurrently with Parliament.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। 42वें संविधान संशोधन से पहले शिक्षा राज्य सूची में थी, इसलिए केंद्र की सामान्य विधायी भूमिका सीमित थी। 1976 में शिक्षा समवर्ती सूची में आई, जिसके बाद संसद और राज्य विधानमंडल दोनों शिक्षा से संबंधित कानून बना सकते हैं। तीसरा कथन गलत है: राज्यों ने अपनी सारी शक्ति नहीं खोई; वे शिक्षा पर विधायी और प्रशासनिक भूमिका बनाए रखते हैं, जबकि केंद्रीय कानून से टकराव होने पर अनुच्छेद 254 लागू हो सकता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Before 1976, school education was in the State List, restricting Central legislation. Shifting education to the Concurrent List enabled central laws like the RTE Act. Statement III is incorrect because State Governments retain broad legislative and administrative powers over education concurrently with Parliament.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Right to Education Act, 2009, is not applicable to institutions offering exclusively religious instruction, such as Madrasas and Vedic Pathshalas.
Reason (R): Article 28(1) prohibits any religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: The RTE Act excludes institutions providing exclusively religious instruction because they do not impart formal elementary education. While Article 28(1) separately prohibits religious instruction in State-maintained institutions, the exclusion of religious institutions like Madrasas under the RTE Act stems from preserving minority educational rights under Article 30, making both statements true independently.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। स्रोत के अनुसार केवल धार्मिक शिक्षा देने वाले संस्थानों को RTE अधिनियम के दायरे से बाहर रखा गया है, क्योंकि वे औपचारिक प्रारंभिक शिक्षा प्रदान करने वाले संस्थानों की श्रेणी में नहीं आते। अनुच्छेद 28(1) राज्य निधि से पूर्णतः संचालित संस्थानों में धार्मिक शिक्षा पर रोक लगाता है, लेकिन यह अलग संवैधानिक नियम है। इसलिए दोनों कथन सही माने गए हैं, पर कारण अभिकथन की सीधी व्याख्या नहीं करता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The RTE Act excludes institutions providing exclusively religious instruction because they do not impart formal elementary education. While Article 28(1) separately prohibits religious instruction in State-maintained institutions, the exclusion of religious institutions like Madrasas under the RTE Act stems from preserving minority educational rights under Article 30, making both statements true independently.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 19(1)(g) (Right to practice profession or occupation)

questions.question_english: An aided linguistic minority school wishes to transition to an English-medium curriculum exclusively, dropping the linguistic minority language from its curriculum. According to Supreme Court interpretations of Article 30:

questions.explanation_english: A linguistic minority institution derives its protection under Article 30(1) read with Article 29(1) specifically to conserve its distinct language and culture.
